content.title: Pure-Go HTML to PDF, no browser
content.lede: A clean-room, stdlib-first work-alike of the wkhtmltopdf CLI that turns server-generated HTML into multi-page PDFs (or PNG/JPEG) entirely in-process. MVP v0.1.0: phases 0-9 of the canonical plan are implemented, with committed samples under output/.

content.heading: Design principles
items: From scratch: the whole pipeline, load to PDF write, lives in this repository. No binding to wkhtmltopdf, Qt, or WebKit, and no third-party PDF/HTML/CSS API or SaaS service.
Stdlib by default: runtime deps are the Go standard library plus one documented exception, github.com/go-text/typesetting, for OpenType shaping.
No browser, no cgo: no Chrome or WebKit process is spawned, and CGO_ENABLED=0 builds produce statically linked binaries with no runtime library requirements.
Deterministic output: identical input bytes and settings produce identical PDF bytes, so builds are cacheable and output diffs are trustworthy.
Report-grade scope: an allowlisted HTML model and a documented CSS subset, with the compatibility matrix as the normative per-property contract.
Two surfaces: the gowkhtmltopdf and gowkhtmltoimage CLI binaries, plus an idiomatic Go library API in the root gowkhtmltopdf package (NewConverter, NewImageConverter).

items.title: Invoices and statements
items.body: Server-generated report templates: multi-section documents, tables with colspan, repeated table headers, and page-break-* control.

items.title: Structured PDFs
items.body: Text headers/footers with [page]-style placeholders, TOC objects, PDF outlines, internal and external links, copies and collate.

items.title: Not: full CSS or browser layout
items.body: Flex and grid are partial, floats and positioned layout are lite, and some selectors are limited. The compatibility matrix states exactly what is supported.

items.title: Not: JavaScript or pixel parity
items.body: <script> content is stripped at load and JS flags such as --enable-javascript are accepted with warnings. Output is not a pixel-identical WebKit or wkhtmltopdf clone.

sections.heading: 1. Load: internal/load
sections.body: Turns a file path, HTTP(S) URL, data: URI, or stdin into bytes. Local file access is denied by default and opens only with --enable-local-file-access or the equivalent settings key; --allow prefixes permit selective paths. HTTP fetches honor cookies and auth and enforce connect/response timeouts, a max redirect count, and a max body size.

sections.heading: 2. Parse and style: internal/html and internal/css
sections.body: The allowlisted HTML tokenizer builds a tree, then the CSS engine applies its subset (boxes, margins/padding/borders, tables, lists, images, colors, page-break-*) with a real cascade.
bullets: Inline and linked stylesheets are applied only when permitted.
Character entities are unescaped via the stdlib.

sections.heading: 3. Layout: internal/layout
sections.body: Resolves styles and runs block, inline, and table layout to produce a display list of text, rectangles, images, and links, ready for painting.

sections.heading: 4. Paginate, TOC, outline: internal/convert
sections.body: Splits the display list across pages using page size, margins, orientation, and page-break-* rules; draws text headers and footers with placeholders such as [page] and [topage]; builds TOC pages with a two-iteration page-count fixpoint and reorders them first; and assembles PDF outline bookmarks via internal/outline.

sections.heading: 5. Write: internal/pdf or internal/imageout
sections.body: PDF mode writes PDF 1.4 with zlib Flate streams, an embedded Liberation Sans subset with /Widths in 1000 units/em, link annotations, and a valid xref. Image mode rasterizes the same display list to PNG or JPEG. Both paths are orchestrated by internal/convert.

content.title: A kvetch: this is not a browser
content.body: gowkhtmltopdf implements a report-grade subset of HTML and CSS and deliberately has no JavaScript runtime. If you need full flexbox parity, interactive scripts, or pixel-identical WebKit output, use a real browser engine. This project is the fast, deterministic, static-binary choice for controlled documents such as invoices and statements.
